item.title: FAA Approves DoorDash Delivery Drones, Humans Will Still Handle Most Orders
item.description: DoorDash Inc. is building its own delivery drones and has gained the necessary approvals to operate them commercially, the latest in its effort to delegate more orders to robots as a way of cutting delivery times.

item.title: JPMorgan Sees Treasury Avoiding Bond Sales Tweak Due to Midterms
item.description: The US Treasury will avoid rattling bond markets ahead of crucial midterm elections, holding off on changes that would introduce the possibility of bigger bond sales in its quarterly refunding statement next week, according to JPMorgan Chase and Co. strategists.

item.title: Wall Street Races to Sell SpaceX-Linked Products as Stock Sinks
item.description: Wall Street is racing to roll out complex investment products tied to SpaceX shares that aim to shield buyers from future losses amid a sharp selloff following its market debut.

item.title: Hermès, Kering Record Stock Spread Highlights Diverging Paths
item.description: Shares of Hermès International SCA and Kering SA diverged by a record margin on Wednesday, marking a dramatic reversal in fortunes for the two luxury goods makers as fresh earnings underscored their contrasting trajectories.

item.title: Zijin Gold’s Allied Deal Scrapped in Favor of $295 Million Stake
item.description: Zijin Gold International Co.’s deal to acquire Canada’s Allied Gold Corp. has been scrapped, with the Chinese mining company opting instead to invest about $295 million in the African-focused gold producer.

item.title: Czech Policymaker Seidler Leaning Toward Holding Rates in August
item.description: Czech central banker Jakub Seidler said he is inclined to leave interest rates unchanged next week, taking more time to gauge the domestic and global drivers of inflation.

item.title: Pakistan, Bangladesh Pay $1 Billion More for LNG as Hormuz Stays Closed
item.description: A switch to more expensive spot cargoes is eroding the cost advantage of the super-chilled fuel.

item.title: London Population Declines as Living Costs Drive Residents Away
item.description: London’s population dropped for the first time since the 1980s, excluding a brief exodus during the pandemic, in a sign people are being priced out of the UK capital.

item.title: Microsoft Faces UK Probe Over Copilot-Linked Price Hikes
item.description: The UK’s consumer and antitrust watchdog is investigating whether Microsoft Corp. misled customers into paying more for its productivity tools software subscriptions after adding its Copilot AI product to the suite.

item.title: Palantir’s New Rivals in Europe Seize the Sovereignty Opening
item.description: European startups aim to replace the US software company

item.title: US and Canada and tariffs
item.description: Trump plans a 50% levy on about $20 billion of Canadian imports

item.title: Fed Watchers Gird for a Lesson on Reading Warsh in High-Stakes Rate Call
item.description: The US central bank is expected to hold, but a hike can’t be ruled out.

item.title: NextEra, Brookfield to Build $100 Billion Kentucky Data Campus
item.description: NextEra Energy Inc., the largest US power utility, is teaming up with Brookfield on a more than $100 billion transformation of a shuttered Cold War uranium-enrichment facility in Kentucky into a data center campus with a generating plant.

item.title: UBS Says Swiss Zero Rate Has Important Impact on Domestic Bank
item.description: The prospect that the Swiss National Bank will keep its key interest rate at zero for an extended period is ushering in potentially lower profitability for the nation’s lenders, not least UBS Group AG.

item.title: GoTo Posts Second Straight Profit After Cost Cuts Kick In
item.description: GoTo Group reported its second consecutive quarter of net income, boosting the Indonesian ride-hailing and food delivery company’s efforts to navigate a challenging consumer market and a looming cut to ride-hailing commissions.

item.title: Verizon Fiber Partners to Invest $1.5 Billion In Network Venture
item.description: Bain Capital and Tillman Global Holdings are making a $1.5 billion investment in Eaton Fiber, a telecom operator providing fiber-optic network capacity to Verizon Communications Inc.

item.title: AI Investment Boom Faces Reality Check From Markets and Regulators
item.description: After months of asking who can spend the most, investors are increasingly asking a different question.

item.title: Markets Brace for One of the Most Uncertain Fed Days in Years
item.description: A chorus of investors say a rate hike is in the cards.

item.title: Hermès’ Chief Tracks China’s Pork Prices to Gauge Handbag Market
item.description: When it comes to gauging the possibility of a sales rebound for his luxury group in China, Hermès Executive Chairman Axel Dumas turns to an unusual metric: pork prices.

item.title: Irish Economy Rebounds With 3.9% Growth After Early-Year Slump
item.description: Ireland’s economy rebounded following a slump at the start of the year, while Belgium failed to grow, offering mixed signals for the euro zone as it grapples with the fallout from the Iran war.

item.title: Nvidia Partner Quanta Seeks Up to $2.2 Billion From Offering
item.description: Artificial-intelligence server maker Quanta Computer Inc. is seeking to raise as much as $2.19 billion from a sale of global depositary shares, in an offering that may be the biggest Taiwanese stock sale in 19 years.

item.title: Ares $29 Billion Private Credit Fund Sees Uptick in Non-Accruals
item.description: Ares Management Corp.’s $29 billion flagship private credit fund reported an increase in troubled investments in the second quarter, as the industry continues to grapple with exposure to businesses vulnerable to advances in artificial intelligence.

item.title: DJI Debuts Long-Awaited Osmo 4P Camera, But US Creators Can’t Buy It
item.description: Chinese drone maker DJI is rolling out its latest product, a $700 mechanically stabilized camera, pressing ahead with global launches while its products remain locked out of the US market following a federal ban last year.

item.title: Aramco Mulls New Oil Pricing for Asia as Houthis Threaten Flows
item.description: Saudi Aramco is preparing a new selling price for oil loaded at Egypt’s Mediterranean port of Sidi Kerir for delivery to Asia after attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants elevated risks in the Red Sea.

item.title: EU Will Support Cities That Want to Curb Short-Term Rentals
item.description: The European Union is preparing measures that will help cities clamp down on short-term rental operators like Airbnb, as Brussels aims to tackle the problem of housing affordability and supply.

item.title: ‘Mr. Brexit’ Leaves Mizuho and UK After Running FICC Strategy
item.description: Jordan Rochester, who made his name as one of the UK’s most recognized financial commentators during the country’s split from the European Union, has left Mizuho Bank Ltd. to pursue a position overseas.

item.title: ASMPT Chief Sees AI Equipment Demand Intact as Bubble Fears Rise
item.description: Chip gear maker ASMPT Ltd.’s top boss said that long-term demand for AI-driven equipment remains firmly intact, pushing back against against growing investor fears of an AI bubble.

item.title: Ukraine Says It Hit Major Rosneft Refinery in Russia’s Ryazan
item.description: Ukraine says it attacked a refinery owned by Russia’s largest oil producer Rosneft PJSC overnight, its first strike on a major oil-processing facility in nearly two weeks.

item.title: Microsoft, Meta Earnings Face a Market Growing Skeptical of AI
item.description: Microsoft Corp. and Meta Platforms Inc. are about to test investors’ diminishing patience for Big Tech’s profligate spending on artificial intelligence and the dwindling cash positions that are the result of it.

item.title: Turkey Lifts Milling Wheat Export Ban as Record Harvest Expected
item.description: The Turkish government gave the green light to milling wheat exports after a year-and-a-half pause.
